t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on deep navy. Top-left: a small label, a large light-weight off-white sans headline in sentence case and a light subhead. Below, a three-column table with small uppercase headers and hairline row rules, numbered rows in mono, for <CONTENT>. A vertical steel-blue double-line riser pipe runs down between the first two columns, with a P&ID gate valve and ball valve branching into every row, and thin pale blue-white pipes routing across to the last column. Larger mono figures inline. Flat blueprint line art, no shading.
signature_idea: Severity rows hang off one steel-blue riser, each with its own valve, so the table reads as a service line that branches by urgency.
strengths: the riser makes a plain service table into a process diagram
inline mono figures make the response times pop
navy, one steel-blue accent, light headline and mono numbers are on-brand
rows stay legible and evenly spaced
weaknesses: secondary white pipes loop over text and add clutter without meaning
row 05 has no response or follow-up, so the pipe ends on an empty row
invented response times and standards references
rounded pipe bends are busy against square table rules
brand_fit_why: Navy blueprint with one steel-blue riser, light headline, mono figures and hairline rules fit the brand, but the extra looping pipes add noise.
